premises.rule: Never fire-and-forget goroutines: every goroutine must have lifecycle management (tracking and shutdown via WaitGroup, errgroup, or context).
Do not discard returned results or errors (no `_ = expensiveOp()`); every result must be checked or explicitly handled.
No I/O operations inside loops; batch operations instead - fetch once, modify in memory, save once.
No hardcoded secrets: API keys, passwords, and credentials must come from environment variables or a secret store, never from source code.
No silent failures: errors must be handled specifically or propagated with added context; empty catch/if branches that swallow errors are forbidden.
Do not use panic() for control flow or recoverable errors in library or handler code; return errors instead.
Service, manager, or handler layers must add value beyond simple delegation; a layer that only forwards calls to a single dependency (>80% delegation) must be deleted.
Repositories are pure CRUD and must not contain business logic such as switch-based state transitions, pricing calculations, or domain decisions.
Errors must be propagated with added context using fmt.Errorf and %w; returning err bare from an if err != nil branch loses the operation context.
context.Context must be the first parameter of any function that performs blocking I/O or network calls.
Preallocate slices when the final size is known before the loop (make([]T, 0, len(items))) to avoid repeated growth allocations.
Do not commit placeholder methods that always return a not-implemented error or throw; implement, remove, or mark them unavailable.
